scenarios.label: Q41 AO3400A at 2.5 V VGS (selected, 25 C max)

reasons: the UCC24624 linear regulator keeps sourcing into REG while the crowbar pulls it down; the constant-current column is a sensitivity, not a guaranteed bound
no component tolerance band is applied to R44 or the REG capacitors
Q41 is the selected AO3400A, but selection is not qualification: its Rds(on) is the datasheet max at 2.5 V VGS and 25 C, with no SOA curve at the turn-on crossing and no self-heating
the discharge model starts with Q41 already on; the gate slewing through R43 delays the 11 V connection, so the quoted time is a floor
turn-on propagation of Q41 and the UVLO-to-VG transient are not modelled

crowbar.note: headline uses the selected AO3400A at its 2.5 V VGS maximum; the 1.5 ohm row is the old 2N7002-class placeholder and must not be quoted as the design number

repetition.basis: UVLO-only capacitor energy x rate; NOT a repetition approval. Full hold/injection is in r44_selection

crowbar_pulse.temperature_note: CRCW-HP vendor curve is archived and conditionally screened; mounted temperature rise and Q41 thermal behavior remain UNVERIFIED
crowbar_pulse.energy_scope: legacy values end at UVLO; r44_selection integrates full hold

source_evidence.method: PDF vector ordinate, visually matched to CRCW1206-HP legend; graph readout, not vendor numeric table

r44_selection.continuous_rating_condition: Rth <= 110 K/W; mounted PCB thermal resistance unverified

land_comparison_mm.status: compatible overlap, not identical to vendor land; assembly check open

assumptions.note: C tolerance, Rds and constant injection are screening assumptions, not full-temperature guarantees

energy.integration_scope: entire hold, not stopped at REG UVLO

hold_sensitivity.note: 95 mA is the VREG=8 V current-limit anchor; the VREG=0 short-circuit anchor and the allowed-current table are in tools/reg_hold.py; no indefinite crowbar approval

open_items: actual REG current and controller dissipation throughout latched fault
mounted thermal resistance, temperature derating and repetition profile
Q41 transient SOA and measured shutdown waveforms

reg_hold.allowed_continuous_basis: conditional equation result at the JEDEC RthJA; actual mounted RthJA is unknown. Neither a 15 V current bound nor a safe limit or transient hold time

bench_bias_limit.basis: initial instrument setting only; main power off during the fault experiments; the bias carries IVDDRUN (1.5 mA max) plus the gate charge of a normally switching pair, not a 100 A load.  40 mA was rejected: at 40 mA a mounted Rth 1.5x worse than the JEDEC value would sit exactly on the 125 C limit
bench_bias_limit.rule: record the actual ambient and limit in reg_hold_bench_record.csv; do not automatically set current from the conditional thermal table. Record actual VDD and PSU current-limit state: a drooping rail or CC event cannot validate shutdown at regulated 15 V. No hold duration is approved

decision.scenario_summary: at the 95 mA current-limit anchor the IC dissipates 1.405 W, i.e. 152 K above ambient (177 C at 25 C), above TJ max in the 25 C reference case; not a 15 V bound
decision.foldback_summary: at the 13 mA short-circuit anchor it would dissipate 0.217 W and reach 48 C at 25 C, but the datasheet does not specify the curve between 8 V and 0 V
required: measure I_REG against V_REG at the board's 15 V bias before any hold longer than the bench limit (row H4)
keep the REG crowbar: it is the only path that crosses UVLO in ~12 us
if the foldback is not proven on the bench, add a latched bias cut for the long hold; the crowbar alone is not a long-hold answer
a bias cut must be latched and reset only deliberately, and the gate state and re-arm sequence have to be re-checked, not assumed

cutting the bias is not enough by itself: the recorded pass condition for the bias-cut experiment is that VDD does not come back up through the SR drains or the output (row H5), because a raised VDD can look like a reset or hold the IC half-alive

open_items: IREGSC is specified at VVDD = 12 V; the board runs 15 V and the short-circuit current there is not specified
IVDDRUN is specified at 12 V; its value at 15 V is not bounded by this calculation

R44 itself dissipates I^2*R = 42 mW at 95 mA; the 1.4 W figure is the controller's, not the resistor's, and the resistor's resistance drift at that level is not modelled (it changes the equilibrium by <1%)
gate charge during the ~12 us transition is not in the steady-state sum; it is a single event of order Qg(sync)*VREG per FET
RthJA is a JEDEC-board, still-air number; the validation board is small and its mounted value is unverified
the die thermal impedance Zth(t) is not in the datasheet, so no transient hold time can be derived, only the steady-state bound
no hardware was available this round: every number here is a datasheet condition-specific value or arithmetic, not a 15 V bound

q41_selection.rds_basis: 3.0 V sits between the 2.5 and 4.5 V datasheet columns; the 2.5 V maximum is used because interpolation is not a guarantee and the 4.5 V column does not apply

turn_on_estimate.status: ESTIMATE from datasheet typ Ciss/Qgd and an assumed Miller plateau; no SOA curve at this crossing is digitised in the repository, so turn-on stress is UNVERIFIED

open_items: SOA at the 11 V turn-on crossing is not checked against a vendor curve
self-heating and the Rds(on) temperature coefficient are not modelled
R44 has a conditional vendor-curve screen; actual repetition and thermal behavior remain open
the 3.3 V harness gives a 3.0 V gate; a 5 V harness would allow the 4.5 V column, but that column is not used here

input_default.limitation: a disconnected or unpowered fault source leaves the board in no-fault; the harness must drive FAULT_IN and a lost-source case belongs in the bench plan

status_output.note: open drain; without an external pull-up the status pin reads low in both states

gate_drive.note: D40 clamps at 5.1 V and does not conduct at either harness level
gate_drive.rds_claim: AO3400A meets 0.1 ohm at the 3.0 V gate the 3.3 V harness produces (datasheet max 0.048 ohm at 2.5 V); a 2N7002-class part at 3.0 V does not

vdd_cut.note: constant-current discharge; the gate stays high until REG UVLO, so a VDD cut alone is not a protection

gate_discharge.note: 4 A sink discharges the gate in nanoseconds; Rgs alone needs tens of microseconds and is the power-down default, not a fault path

sr_branch.reg_to_uvlo_basis: 3.63 V turn-off threshold (slowest of 3.63/4.0/4.25 V), AO3400A Rds(on) 0.048 ohm at 2.5 V VGS

primary_branch_reference.note: not implemented on this board; numbers are for the roadmap equation, from the same datasheet set

not_worst_case_reasons: reg_to_uvlo_s is an RC estimate at the 3.63 V threshold; the regulator keeps sourcing, and the current-limit column is a sensitivity
component tolerances on R44 and the REG capacitors are not applied

observations.finding: The UCC24624 has no enable pin; only REG UVLO or standby turns the gate off. The crowbar therefore targets REG, not VG.

REG holds 139 uJ at 11 V (124 uJ down to the 3.63 V threshold); the 4.7 ohm crowbar reaches UVLO in 12.1 us. That is an estimate covering a low-threshold part, not a fast hard shutdown and not a hardware worst case.
observations.evidence: computed from C4+C5 and references/datasheets/ucc24624.txt VREGOFF min/max

observations.finding: A VDD-only cut takes 75 ms at the 1.5 mA run current -- three orders of magnitude slower.
observations.evidence: computed from C1+C2+C3 and references/datasheets/ucc24624.txt IVDDRUN

observations.finding: A 2N7002-class VG clamp (1.5 ohm) only reaches 2.06 V, above the 1.30 V threshold, so it cannot guarantee the SR FET is off.
observations.evidence: divider against references/datasheets/ucc24624.txt RVG_PU; references/datasheets/bsc010n04ls6.txt VGS(th)

observations.finding: A clamp strong enough to hold VG low (0.02 ohm) makes U1 dissipate 18.5 W while it keeps sourcing.
observations.evidence: computed from references/datasheets/ucc24624.txt RVG_PU and IVGSOURCE

observations.finding: Passive gate decay through Rgs 10k is 60 us tau; the 4 A active sink is what makes the UVLO path fast.
This board is not a 100 A power stage and has no thermal model; it validates the shutdown interface only.
FAULT_IN defaults to no crowbar. A lost or unpowered fault source therefore does not shut the board down; the bench plan has to drive it and test the lost-source case.
observations.evidence: R41 10k to PGND on the fault input

observations.finding: A 3.3 V harness gives Q41 only 3.0 V of gate drive, so the BOM's Rds(on) <= 0.1 ohm has to be quoted at that voltage or the harness has to drive 5 V.
observations.evidence: R40/R41 divider into the Q41 gate; Q41 AO3400A selected, transient qualification open

limits: low-energy validation board, <=10 A and <=5 V output
no thermal model; Rds(on) and Ciss are datasheet typical/max, not measured
Q41 is selected as AO3400A (datasheet in references/) but not qualified: SOA at the turn-on crossing, self-heating and actual R44 repetition/hold conditions are open
